Composition is more hidden. One function changes because another function inside it changes first:

This happens constantly. A temperature changes because position changes. A cost changes because production changes. A population changes because time changes. The outside quantity does not see x directly. It sees an intermediate quantity.

exercise.title: Why is a composite rate a product of two rates?

statement.p: Temperature can change because position changes, and position can change because time changes. In your own words, why must \dfrac{dT}{dt} be the product \dfrac{dT}{dx}\dfrac{dx}{dt}, and what does each factor measure?

hint.p: The outside function never sees x directly. It sees an intermediate quantity, whose own rate must be included.

subsection.title: Why the hypotheses are there
subsection.p: The chain rule assumes that the inside function is differentiable at the point, and that the outside function is differentiable at the inside value. Both assumptions matter.

paragraphs.title: The outside function must be differentiable at the inside value
paragraphs.p: At x=0, the inside value is
But f(u)=|u| is not differentiable at u=0. The composite |x| is not differentiable at x=0. There is no chain rule product to compute there.

paragraphs.title: The inside function must be differentiable at the point
paragraphs.p: The outside function f(u)=u is differentiable everywhere, but g(x)=|x| is not differentiable at x=0. Again the composite is not differentiable at 0.

note.title: Moral
note.p: A composite function can only inherit a derivative through the chain rule when both links in the chain have derivatives at the needed places.

exercise.title: Why must both links in the chain be differentiable?

statement.p: The chain rule needs the inside function differentiable at the point and the outside function differentiable at the inside value. In your own words, why does replacing either link by absolute value at 0 break the composite derivative?

hint.p: A composite can inherit a derivative only through both links. If either link lacks a tangent slope at the needed place, the chain has no product to compute.

exercise.title: Why does the order of composition matter?

statement.p: Usually f(g(x)) and g(f(x)) are different functions, so their derivatives are different as well. In your own words, why must we differentiate from the outside inward while still preserving the original order of the layers?

hint.p: The outside derivative is evaluated at the current inside value. Swapping the layers swaps which function is outside.

statement.p: The same two functions, used in a different order, produce different composites.

warning.title: Chain rule warning
warning.p: Differentiate from the outside inward, but preserve the order in which the function is built.

exercise.title: Why is the chain rule local linear approximation rather than canceling du?

statement.p: The notation \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy}{du}\dfrac{du}{dx} looks like cancellation. In your own words, why is that a useful memory but not the proof, and how do the two linear approximations compose?

hint.p: A small change in x produces an approximate change in u, which then produces an approximate change in y. Multiply the two conversion factors.
